bugs.name: Go to Dashboard from a public status page opens Status Pages management
bugs.summary: The Go to Dashboard link on a public status page opens Status Pages management instead of the monitor dashboard.
bugs.expected: Go to Dashboard should open the monitor dashboard.
bugs.actual: The Go to Dashboard link on a public status page opens Status Pages management instead of the monitor dashboard.
reproSteps: Sign in to Uptime Kuma and open the seeded public status page.
Click Go to Dashboard on that page.
Observe the Status Pages management directory instead of /dashboard.

bugs.name: Status page refresh interval persists below its minimum
bugs.summary: A status page accepts a four-second refresh interval even though its numeric control declares a minimum of five seconds.
bugs.expected: Saving a refresh interval below five seconds should be rejected or constrained to the declared minimum.
bugs.actual: The editor saves 4 and reopening the editor shows 4 persisted.
reproSteps: Create a new status page and open its editor.
Set Refresh Interval to 4 even though the control declares min=5, then save.
Reopen Edit Status Page to confirm 4 persists.

bugs.name: Show Only Last Heartbeat still renders heartbeat history
bugs.summary: A status page saved with Show Only Last Heartbeat enabled still displays Application Entry API’s 34-check heartbeat timeline after reopening the editor and explicitly refreshing its public page.
bugs.expected: When Show Only Last Heartbeat is enabled and saved, the public status page should show only the latest heartbeat/status and omit the historical timeline; this is also the direct promise of the setting’s visible label.
bugs.actual: With Show Only Last Heartbeat enabled, the public status page still showed a heartbeat history strip spanning eight minutes and several checks.
reproSteps: Create a disposable status page with a group containing an existing monitor.
Enable Show Only Last Heartbeat, save, and reopen the public status page.
Observe that the monitor still has a heartbeat history strip spanning several minutes.

bugs.name: Status-page editor preview is compressed and clipped at a mobile viewport
bugs.summary: At 390×844, the status-page editor keeps a desktop-style side-by-side layout: the settings panel consumes most of the viewport and the rendered preview is clipped into a narrow strip. Waiting and horizontal scrolling do not produce a usable combined editor/preview view.
bugs.expected: At a 390×844 viewport, the status-page editor and its rendered preview should remain legible and usable, with the preview adapting to the available width.
bugs.actual: After Next, the settings pane occupied most of the viewport and the preview at the right edge was only a narrow slice: “Create Incident,” “No Services,” and other preview text/buttons were clipped or wrapped across lines. After the editor settled, horizontal scrolling exposed more of the preview only by moving the settings pane offscreen; the preview still did not adapt to the viewport.
reproSteps: Use the supplied authenticated administrator session; set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open /dashboard and select Settings, then Status Pages, then New Status Page.
Create a fresh page with name `MO-STATUS-MOBILE-RESP-CHK-734921` and slug `mo-status-mobile-resp-chk-734921`.
Select Next and inspect the editor at /status/mo-status-mobile-resp-chk-734921?edit.
Wait for the editor to settle, then scroll horizontally to check whether the preview becomes usable without losing the settings pane.

bugs.name: Discarding a status page opens an unnecessary leave-page confirmation
bugs.summary: The status-page editor's Discard action triggers the browser's beforeunload prompt even when there are no edits, requiring an extra confirmation before leaving the editor.
bugs.expected: Discard should leave the editor and restore the saved status page without a browser leave-page confirmation, including when no fields have changed.
bugs.actual: Clicking Discard opens a native beforeunload confirmation with an empty message. Accepting it reloads the status page and restores the saved title. This occurred twice, including with no edits.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open the existing status page at /status/momentic-service-status.
Click Edit Status Page.
Without changing any fields, click Discard.
Observe the browser's native beforeunload confirmation. Accept it to return to the saved status page.

bugs.name: Incident form publishes blank incidents using whitespace-only title and content
bugs.summary: The incident form rejects empty strings but accepts whitespace-only title and content, publishing an incident alert with no visible information.
bugs.expected: Post rejects title or content containing only whitespace, with the same required-field validation used for empty input.
bugs.actual: Post succeeds. The public status page displays a blank incident heading and blank content with a creation date; the whitespace-only incident persists after navigation.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a status page, then click Edit Status Page.
Click Create Incident.
Enter three spaces in both the title and content fields.
Click Post, save the status page, and reopen its public view.

bugs.name: Status page editor overwrites user typing when saved settings finish loading
bugs.summary: Edit Status Page exposes editable fields before saved configuration finishes loading. The delayed load resets the Title mid-typing, silently losing or corrupting the user's changes.
bugs.expected: Editable fields preserve user input, or editing waits until the saved configuration has loaded.
bugs.actual: The saved title is reinserted mid-typing, producing 'QA Status Alternate normal typing change'. Save persists that corrupted title. Filling the Title immediately in one action also resets it entirely to the saved title about one second later; reproduced twice.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a saved status page whose title is QA Status Alternate.
Click Edit Status Page.
Immediately select the Title text and type QA normal typing change at an ordinary typing speed.
Observe the Title after the saved configuration loads about one second later.
Click Save and reopen the public status page.

bugs.name: Pinning an archived incident does not show it prominently on the status page
bugs.summary: Past Incidents' edit dialog allows Pin this incident and persists the setting, but the incident remains only in the archive instead of appearing prominently as the helper promises.
bugs.expected: A pinned incident is displayed prominently on the status page as the Pin setting describes, or pinning is unavailable for resolved incidents.
bugs.actual: The setting remains checked after saving, but no prominent incident alert appears. The incident is shown only under Past Incidents. Reproduced with two archived incidents, including an incident created with valid title/content throughout.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a status page for editing.
Create an incident with a valid title and content, post it, and resolve it.
Under Past Incidents, click Edit for the resolved incident.
Check Pin this incident, click the modal Save, then save the status page.
Open the public page in a fresh unauthenticated browser view and reopen the incident editor for comparison.

bugs.name: Duplicate status-page slug returns a database error instead of validation
bugs.summary: Renaming a status page to an existing slug bypasses uniqueness validation and forwards the resulting database error to the editor.
bugs.expected: Block the save with a clear message that the slug is already taken and another slug must be chosen.
bugs.actual: Saving an existing status page with another page's slug reaches the SQLite uniqueness constraint. The failure is returned through error.message to the editor rather than a clear slug-already-taken validation message.
reproSteps: Sign in with at least two existing status pages with distinct slugs.
Open one status page and click Edit Status Page.
Change Slug to the slug of the other existing page, blur the field, and click Save.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Only the core failure described in this reference is accepted; the stronger original subclaims remain unestablished.

bugs.name: Past Incidents groups events under a different date from their displayed creation date
bugs.summary: In America/Los_Angeles, status-page incidents created in the evening are grouped under the following UTC day, while their timestamps use the local day. The date heading therefore contradicts both incident timestamps.
bugs.expected: The grouping heading uses the same date/timezone as the incident timestamps displayed beneath it.
bugs.actual: The page /status/bb-sp-renamed groups both incidents under October 9, 2026, but displays Created: 2026-10-08 18:05:12 and Created: 2026-10-08 18:08:12, with October 8 update timestamps too. Parent independently observed the mismatch after reload.
reproSteps: Use a browser in America/Los_Angeles during an evening where the UTC date is the following day (reproduced October 8, 2026 at 18:05–18:08).
Create a status page, add a monitor, and save.
Edit the page, create and post an incident, resolve it, and save.
View the public status page's Past Incidents section; repeat with a second incident and reload.

reviewedVariants.name: Past incident date headings disagree with incident timestamps
reviewedVariants.summary: The public status page groups past incidents under a UTC date while showing their timestamps in browser local time, placing incidents beneath the wrong displayed day.
reviewedVariants.expected: The incident date heading and timestamps use the same timezone; these incidents belong under October 8, 2026.
reviewedVariants.actual: Past Incidents shows 'October 9, 2026' above incidents with Created '2026-10-08 21:21:40' and '2026-10-08 21:22:26'. The mismatch persists after reload.
reproSteps: Use a browser in America/Los_Angeles timezone and sign in.
Create or edit a status page.
During a time when the UTC and local calendar dates differ (verified October 9 2026 04:21 UTC / October 8 21:21 local), create and post an incident.
Resolve the incident, save the status page, and reload its public view.
Compare the Past Incidents date heading with the Created and Last Updated timestamps.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Browser local date differs from configured timestamp timezone or raw timestamp parsing.
